title: Complex mixture toxicity in E. Crypticus: organic emerging contaminants, silver sulphide nanoparticles and the limits of predictive models
content:
Abstract
A wide range of emerging contaminants (ECs) such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, antibiotics, estrogens, personal care products, pesticides, plasticizers coexist in soil. However, chemical exposures and their ecological impacts are generally described with a focus on single chemicals. Hence, this study examined the mixture toxicity of eight organic ECs from numerous sources, i.e. Diclofenac, Ciprofloxacin, Ethinylestradiol, Diphenyl Ether, Terbutryn, Diuron, Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) and Anthracene in soil on the reproduction of E. crypticus. DEHP and Anthracene showed toxic effects at their environmental occurrence values. Mixture toxicity of 8 pollutants for reproduction was significantly higher (EC50 6.44 ± 0.66 mg/kg) compared to their individual toxicities. The results indicated a synergistic effect of these pollutants in soil, and the Toxic Unit (TU) also supported the synergistic calculation. The presence of silver sulfide nanoparticles, another EC in metallic structure, at their no-effect concentration (NOEC) (5 mg/kg) significantly increases the mixture toxicity of organic ECs (4.0 ± 0.59 mg/kg). Therefore, it can be speculated that the presence of nanoparticles could pose a threat to the toxicity of other ECs. The results showed that ECs with high toxic potential in the soil environment must be regularly monitored to avoid detrimental effects in the soil. Therefore, mixture effects should be considered in risk assessment methods for polluted soils. However, this study showed that concentration addition (CA) predictive model has potential to underestimate complex ECs mixtures. It is further suggested to investigate on predictive toxicity models on complex mixtures in the soil environment.
